name: Typescript Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in typescript work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in typescript work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Prefer the simplest typescript approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
2. When typescript decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Surface known limitations of a chosen typescript approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
4. Measure before optimizing any typescript bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. Keep typescript outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
6. Prefer explicit, readable typescript solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. State assumptions about typescript explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
8. Validate typescript outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. When typescript guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
10. Keep typescript changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
11. Document any non-obvious typescript decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
12. When multiple typescript strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting typescript assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop typescript edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated typescript concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new typescript abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic typescript advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these typescript guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
